content: For decades, we've organized digital information the same way we organize physical objects: by putting them in containers. Files go in folders. Emails go in inboxes. Notes go in notebooks. This metaphor served us well when storage was expensive and retrieval was manual.

But containers are fundamentally limiting. They force hierarchical thinking onto information that is inherently networked. A note about a conversation with a client belongs in the client folder, the project folder, and the meeting notes folder simultaneously. We've been forcing square pegs into round holes.

The rise of AI changes everything. When machines can understand content semantically, the container becomes obsolete. Why file a document when the system can surface it based on meaning, context, and relevance?

This isn't just about better search. It's a fundamental shift in how we relate to information. Instead of asking "where did I put that?", we ask "what do I need right now?" The system becomes an extension of thought rather than a filing cabinet.

We're building tools that embrace this shift. Unbody treats all your content—documents, images, videos, conversations—as a unified knowledge space. No folders. No manual organization. Just intelligent retrieval based on what matters.
The container era served us well. But it's time to move on. The future of information is fluid, contextual, and deeply personal. We're excited to be building it.
Quick update on what we shipped this week at Unbody.
We completely rewrote our TypeScript SDK from scratch. The new version features full type inference, tree-shakeable modules, and a much cleaner API surface. Upgrade guide is live in the docs.

Key improvements:
- 60% smaller bundle size
- Automatic retry with exponential backoff
- Streaming support for large responses
- Better error messages with actionable suggestions
I gave a talk at the AI Engineers meetup about semantic search patterns. Covered the tradeoffs between dense vs sparse retrieval and when hybrid approaches make sense. Slides are up on our blog.
We merged 12 community PRs this week. Huge thanks to everyone contributing. Special shoutout to @devuser for the improved caching layer—it cut our test suite time by 40%.
Next week we're focusing on the dashboard redesign. Early mockups look promising. Stay tuned.
Join us for an evening of building, learning, and connecting with fellow AI enthusiasts.

**When:** March 20, 2024, 6:00 PM - 10:00 PM
**Where:** Unbody HQ, Amsterdam
**Who:** Developers, designers, and curious minds interested in AI
We're hosting a hands-on hack night focused on practical LLM applications. Whether you're building your first chatbot or fine-tuning models for production, there's something here for you.

The evening kicks off with a short intro to Unbody's API and some inspiration from projects built by the community. Then it's heads-down building time. We'll have mentors floating around to help debug, brainstorm, and push your ideas forward.
Pizza and drinks provided. Bring your laptop and an idea you want to explore.
At our last hack night, teams built everything from a recipe generator that works with whatever's in your fridge to a tool that summarizes Slack channels. The energy was incredible.
Space is limited to 30 people. Sign up on our Luma page. See you there.
